messages:
alice: Quick heads-up — noticed a regression in KV cache tail latency after the shard-handoff change. p50 ~ same, p95+p99 up ~30%. Anybody else see this?
ben: yup. Saw it in the nightly perf snapshot. Heatmap shows all-reduce spikes during decode steps.
carla: perf-bot posted flamegraphs in #perf-dash, but attaching key snippet here.
perf-bot: flamegraph link: https://perf.example/fg/1768001234 (private) :mag:
ben: profiler dump (short):
```
step 420: decode tokens 128 -> 512
all-reduce (KV sync): 2.1ms -> 8.7ms
kernel memcpy: 0.9ms -> 3.4ms
```
carla: hypothesis: shard handoff moves hot KV slices between PP devices during pipeline stage boundaries, causing unexpected synchronous all-reduces and blocking kernels. TP placement used to keep hot KV on same device.
david: +1. Also saw extra kernel selection path taken — fallback to generic matmul kernel when seq len mismatch hits. That increases compute and prevents overlap.
alice: any quick mitigations we can A/B? can we force local pinning for hot prefixes or prefer TP affinity?
ben: experiment idea: 1) pin hot prefixes to replica set (reduce handoff), 2) change batching heuristic to prefer smaller batches while handoff active, 3) force async all-reduce NVLINK when available.
carla: I'll try (1) with canary config. patch: 
```
kv_shard_handoff:
  disabled_for_prefixes: ["usr", "session:"]
batching:
  prefer_latency: true
```
carla: starting canary (1 node) now.
ci-bot: canary deploy started: infra/job/kv-handoff-canary/1768001234 — logs streaming
ben: also plumbed a small profiler hook that logs kernel selection reason (shape mismatch / quant path / fallback) — can share output in 10m.
alice: perfect. if this reduces p99 we'll push revert for handoff change and investigate kernel path deeper. thx all :thumbsup:
